course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 8

unit.title: Interpreting and Discussing Results
unit.blurb: Frequency diagrams, time series graphs, stem-and-leaf diagrams and pie charts, choosing a representation, and comparing data with averages and the range.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Draw and interpret frequency diagrams for grouped discrete and continuous data.

O2.t: Draw and interpret time series graphs and describe trends.

O3.t: Draw and interpret stem-and-leaf diagrams, and find the median, mode and range from them.

O4.t: Draw and interpret pie charts, calculating angles and frequencies.

O5.t: Choose a suitable graph or chart for a set of data and explain the choice.

O6.t: Use the mean, median, mode and range to compare sets of data and draw conclusions.

p: When there are lots of different values, group them into **classes** of equal width, such as 0 ≤ t < 10, 10 ≤ t < 20.
A **frequency diagram** for continuous data has bars that touch, with the classes on a continuous scale.
The **modal class** is the class with the highest frequency. Add all the frequencies to find the total.
A time of exactly 10 minutes goes in 10 ≤ t < 20, not 0 ≤ t < 10.

p: A **time series graph** shows how something changes over time. Time goes on the horizontal axis. Plot the points and join them with straight lines.
Describe the **trend**: increasing, decreasing or staying about the same, and any pattern that repeats (such as seasons).
The lines between points only show the trend; values between months may not be exact.

p: A **stem-and-leaf diagram** keeps every value. The **stem** is the tens digit and the **leaf** is the units digit. Leaves are written in order, and a **key** explains how to read it.
Because the data is in order, it is easy to find the median, mode and range.
2 | 3 might mean 23, 2.3 or 230. Always read the key.

p: A **pie chart** shows how a whole is shared. The whole circle is **360°**.
Angle for a group = frequency ÷ total × 360°. With 40 people, each person is 360 ÷ 40 = 9°.

p: **Bar chart**: compare categories. **Frequency diagram**: grouped continuous data. **Pie chart**: parts of a whole. **Line graph / time series**: change over time. **Stem-and-leaf**: show all values in order. **Scatter graph**: compare two variables.
Only use a pie chart when the categories make up one whole.
